conviction_note: Jyske pre-released the whole Q3 P&L and balance sheet and raised the 2026 EPS guide to DKK 78-87 by inside-information announcement on 2026-10-12 (stock +0.56% that day). Barclays put the top of the new range about 4% above consensus EPS, so the market already expects the upper half, and nothing sourced says the guide or the DKK 3bn buyback (74% done, on pace) changes on 28 October. The two findings offset at about zero, p_up is 50, and the release's only open lines are the Q3 CET1 ratio (H1 15.7% against a ~15% target) and the guide's wording.

already_public.what: Full Q3 2026 and Q1-Q3 P&L and balance sheet pre-released: Q3 net profit DKK 1,278m, Q1-Q3 DKK 3,680m (index 92), NII Q3 2,270 vs 2,177 in Q2, loan impairments -50m, core expenses 1,605m incl. 16m one-off
2026 guidance raised to net profit DKK 4.7-5.2bn / EPS DKK 78-87 (from 4.3-5.1bn / 71-85)
Barclays: Q3 net profit 8% above its forecast, costs above consensus, upgrade mainly lower credit losses; top of new range ~4% above consensus 2026 EPS; overweight, TP DKK 1,340
Formuepleje acquisition approved by the competition authority, completion expected 2 November 2026; ~0.1% of REA net capital consumption, ~DKK 0.1bn integration costs, EPS accretive from 2028
Buyback status: DKK 2.21bn of DKK 3bn repurchased (2,292,311 shares, 3.94% of share capital) as of week 43; programme runs to 29 January 2027

new_in_release.expect: most likely reiterated at DKK 78-87, possibly narrowed. Q4 implied 1.02-1.52bn against Q3 1.28bn and Q4 2025 1.42bn. The market already leans to the upper half (Barclays: top end ~4% above consensus), so a narrowing to the upper half is roughly priced. Sign unknown.

Q3 CET1 ratio and capital commentary (H1 15.7%; ~15% CET1 target per secondary summaries; Formuepleje consumes ~0.1pt). A capital-distribution signal is the only capital lever, and Jyske's practice is to announce distribution with the annual report in February. Unknown, small.
no change: the P&L was pre-released in full on 2026-10-12

bar: The company's own pre-release and raised guide (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b2b1a5023b7ec4cc74a6a28ec0f7d852a&lang=en&src=listed). findings.finding: Disclosed net short positions in Jyske rose from 0.61% to 0.83% of shares (position date 2026-10-26), so sellers are adding in the days before a print whose P&L is already public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no observed history of the short register mattering for Jyske; the aggregate has been small
findings.why_not_priced: It is public on the register and already in the baseline's lean (short_building -0.44). The increment is ~DKK 0.14bn, about 1.3 days of turnover, so it is neither crowded fuel nor big enough to be informative. If it were a real informed bet, the stock would be underperforming its Danish bank peers, and it is not: since 2026-10-12 Jyske is -2.1%, Danske -2.8%, Ringkjøbing -2.4% (Yahoo daily closes).

findings.finding: The DKK 3bn buyback is buying about DKK 11-12m a day (week 43: 56,352 shares, DKK 58.9m), roughly 12% of daily turnover, with ~DKK 0.79bn left to 29 January 2027, so it keeps steady bid support through the print day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: the stock has drifted down with Danish bank peers since 12 October despite the buyback; constant support, not an event
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the programme was announced in February and is reported weekly. Its only relevance is that buyback flow under Safe Harbour continues through the print and damps the downside tail. If the market had priced more than that, Jyske would have outperformed peers since 12 October, and it has only matched them.

outside_window.finding: Formuepleje completion effective 2 November 2026 (approx. DKK 0.2bn annual net fees, EPS accretive from 2028), after the exit window
Next capital distribution (new buyback and dividend) customarily announced with the annual report in February; the current DKK 3bn programme runs to 29 January 2027

baseline_tension: Nothing found cuts against the small positive lean (+0.28) or the -4.5% 20-day run-up. The run-up is sector-wide drift shared with Danske and Ringkjøbing, not something specific to Jyske, and the short build is too small to be fuel or signal.
language_note: The Danish-language sources added nothing the English ones did not already carry: every Jyske Bank corporate announcement on the Nasdaq Nordic feed in this period is in English (Danish only for one weekly buyback report, uge 38), and the Danish searches turned up no Børsen or Finans preview

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': confirmed that the pre-released Q3 beat stays out of findings (already_public / rejected_candidates); no size change, because the draft had already excluded it

'You were too small about the move' and the measured ~3.1% median for pre-released periods: abs_move_pct raised from 2.0 to 2.5. It is held below 3 because this is a low-vol bank (20d realised 1.27%/day) whose two prior pre-released report days moved +0.60% (2025-10-29) and -2.18% (2026-02-05)
'Positioning is the thing to beat, not to agree with': the short-building finding shrunk from -0.2 to -0.1, since a negative that restates a public register build is already in the lean
